definition_unchanged: A bag used to carry purchased items.
original_brief: Show a reusable fabric shopping bag upright with two handles and a few purchased items peeking above the opening. Make the flexible sides and carrying handles clearly distinct from a rigid shopping basket. Reject a backpack, paper-only carrier definition, wheeled trolley, or decorative gift bag that obscures the intended shopping use.
proposed_brief: Show a plain open retail shopping bag upright in a three-quarter view, with a tall solid-sided body, two separate loop handles and a visible opening. Preserve the inspected 3dicons dynamic color source. Keep the tall solid body and paired loops visually distinct from the accepted squat slotted shopping basket. Exclude wheels, backpack straps, a closed top, a bow, a gift tag, tissue paper and gift-specific decoration. The illustration does not narrow the definition to a particular material or require visible contents.
rationale: Reusable fabric, flexible sides and visible purchases were depiction choices in the original brief. They are not necessary conditions of the approved broad purchased-goods-carrier definition. The acquired source has an open cavity and paired loops, while the accepted basket is squat, slotted and broad-handled. The source does not establish reusable fabric or a particular material; do not claim either.
limits: An empty generic bag cannot establish shopping use absolutely; gift and shopping bags can share a form.
The inspected source has no gift-specific decoration, brand, text, ribbon or tag.
Source and simulated size review authorize candidate QA only; native cue visibility and the brief revision remain pending independent root review.
No participant recognition study or human subject-matter approval is claimed.
allowed_candidate_adaptations: Use the exact frozen study derivative: crop alpha bounds plus 16 source pixels, then Lanczos reduction to 414 by 512.
Do not redraw, recolor, add contents or handles, change the material, or acquire an unreviewed source variant.
